newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA TOUGHENS LEGISLATION TO FIGHT CRIME.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA TOUGHENS LEGISLATION TO FIGHT CRIME.

text.p: Bulgaria's parliament on Friday adopted on second and final reading amendments to the penal code in a bid to toughen anti-crime laws and stem organised crime and corruption.

The Bulgarian outdated legal system provided only a limited support to efforts by law enforcement agencies to counter soaring crime rate in the adminstrative chaos that followed the end of one-party rule in 1989, officials said.

The amendments are aimed mainly at combating more effectively violent crime, economic fraud, embezzlement and tax evasion, drug trade and smuggling, racketeering and establishment of big organised criminal groups.
Under the amendments tougher jail terms were set for car theft, a big problem in post-communist Bulgaria, and trafficking in people, another spreading type of organised crime.
Parliament also expanded self-defence rights, under which a person, attacked on the territory of his property or in his vehicle can defend himself even through killing the attacker.
Parliament also passed on final reading amendments to a Profiteering Control Bill expanding fines up to 10 million levs.
Bulgaria's new government, which took over on May 21, has made fight against organised crime and corruption a priority.
